sources.text:
Evidence-based career decision support for the Japanese job market.

Your career record stays on your machine, and nothing becomes a fact without your approval.

Record what happened: past work becomes contexts, experiences and checkable evidence, and what you cannot verify stays Unknown.

Approve it: nothing enters your canonical career record until you confirm it, and a number without a source is refused.

Use it: JD matching, a Japanese resume, interview practice and next actions, all quoting only confirmed evidence.

Evidence, not invented scores or career history.

If a fact is not confirmed, it stays Unknown.

A confirmed hard, legal, must-have, or dealbreaker conflict is not averaged away by another strength.

The system does not predict whether you will be hired.

You make the final decision and keep approval control; it does not submit applications or send messages for you.

It runs as a Claude Code and Codex plugin, as a standalone command, and as an optional local GUI, over one Python runtime and one Career Vault.

A plugin never holds its own copy of your career facts; the plugin changes how you reach the core, never what it says.

The model is context, then experience, then evidence, discovered in that order; the order is the design, not a presentation choice.

The career inventory recovers what happened; it does not interpret it, and it never turns a strength or a number into a confirmed fact on your behalf.

The JD changes the lens, never the fact.

No axis is summed, averaged, multiplied, or ranked into a total, and requirement states are Matched, Missing, or Unknown.

A plugin never writes canonical state outside the core contract, so a host cannot approve on your behalf, skip the evidence requirement, or add a fact the CLI would have refused.

The layers run Entry, then Command line, then Application, then Domain, then Local data; dependencies point down and nothing at any layer imports an entry point.

Application owners include onboarding, approvals, sessions, guided_flow, documents and experiences; the domain holds models, validation, vault, routing, proposals, lifecycle, projection, document, render and execution_plans.

The canonical runtime is Python, and every entry point runs that same program against the same Career Vault.

For a multi-Skill host turn the runtime builds a bounded plan; each step uses the skill-open, SOP, skill-report lifecycle and Python never calls an LLM host or another Skill.

The evidence vocabulary keeps Confirmed, Unknown, Contradictory, Stale and Low Confidence apart, and interest_level records preference without changing objective evidence or decision status.

Japan Career Agent is a Career Operating System: it does not decide a career for the user, it accumulates and verifies evidence so the user can make a better decision.

A resume, a Japanese CV, interview answers, JD notes, company research and self-analysis usually live in different chats, documents and memories.

The suite ships 18 specialized skills, split across capture, analysis, decision, document and verification work.

Capture covers the career inventory and ongoing maintenance; analysis covers self-analysis and company research; decision covers JD matching and company battlecards; creation covers document building and Japanese phrasing; verification covers intent, factcheck, challenge and verify.

Illustrative: a generic assistant weights Java 90, English 80 and cloud 95, discounts a work visa at 20, and still reports a blended 82 out of 100 as a good match.

Read on independent axes, the same case keeps the work visa as a missing hard requirement and sets the decision to Review rather than a score.

The document pipeline turns a confirmed evidence pool into a target-specific document model, passes it through a deterministic fidelity gate, and only then renders it.

Governed execution means intent, a bounded plan, skill invocation, execution, verification and factcheck all sit between the user and the canonical record.

Your career should compound, and so should your career memory: local-first, approval-gated, and agent-native.

The knowledge graph links a target role to its contexts, the experiences inside them, and the evidence that makes each experience checkable.

contract.audience: Recruiting and career-industry professionals in the Japanese market
contract.objective: Show why career AI must be built on accumulated, verified, user-approved evidence

content.subtitle: Evidence-based career decision support for the Japanese job market.

slides.headline: The most dangerous moment in career AI is the confident guess

claims.text: The most dangerous moment in career AI is the confident guess

content.body: Resume, Japanese CV, interview answers, JD notes and company research each live apart.
proofs: Every chat starts the agent from zero
A number gets repeated until nobody can source it
The riskiest output is a guess with a confident tone

slides.headline: Career advice needs memory, evidence, and governance

claims.text: Career advice needs memory, evidence, and governance

content.body: One record to remember it, a source to check it, and approval that stays with you.
proofs: Memory: one career record, reused everywhere
Evidence: attach a source, or it stays Unknown
Governance: no fact enters without your yes

slides.headline: Record a career once, reuse it for every task

right.label: Your recorded evidence
items: Confirmed: cloud migration, Java services in production
Unknown: Kubernetes, not in the ledger yet

content.delta: Every requirement resolves to Matched, Missing, or Unknown

slides.headline: A hard conflict is never averaged away

claims.text: A hard conflict is never averaged away

left.label: Generic assistant
items: Work visa scored 20, treated as one weak input
Blended result 82 out of 100, called a good match

right.label: Japan Career Agent
items: Cloud and Java: Matched to confirmed evidence
Work visa: Missing, and it is a hard requirement
Decision: Review, because a hard conflict is not offset

content.delta: A confirmed hard conflict is never averaged into a score
